title: Chicken Larb (Laab Gai) with Toasted Rice and Mint
changes_from_base: Minced chicken is steamed in a little water in a hot pan to 74°C instead of beef, and red onion replaces the shallot for a lighter, brighter larb.
summary: A lighter take on the classic beef larb, made with gently steamed minced chicken and red onion in place of shallot, finished with mint, coriander and toasted rice powder.
equipment: mortar and pestle or spice grinder

ingredients.item: raw jasmine or sticky rice, for toasted rice powder
Thai chilli flakes (or ordinary chilli flakes)
coriander, leaves and tender stems, chopped
long beans or green beans, raw, cut into lengths

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Toast the raw rice in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring often, for 6-10 minutes until it's deep golden and smells nutty. Cool it fully, then grind to a coarse powder. This larb follows the same method as the classic beef version, but with minced chicken steamed gently to 74°C instead of beef, and red onion in place of the shallot for a lighter, brighter dressing.

steps.title: Mix the dressing
steps.text: Stir the red onion, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chilli flakes together in a large bowl, cutting back on the chilli flakes if you want a milder result. Set this aside while the chicken cooks. Red onion gives a crisper bite and a milder flavour than shallot, which suits the lighter character of chicken larb.

steps.title: Steam the chicken
steps.text: Heat the large pan over medium-high until hot, add the water, then the chicken, and stir constantly, breaking up any lumps, for 3-5 minutes. Cook until no raw-looking bits remain and the chicken reaches 74°C in the centre; the splash of water steams it gently from within so it stays soft rather than drying out. Transfer it to the dressing while it's still warm, so it drinks up the lime and fish sauce.

steps.title: Add the herbs
steps.text: Stir in most of the coriander, mint and spring onion along with two-thirds of the toasted rice powder. Taste and adjust - it should come across as tangy, salty and lightly hot - adding more rice powder for extra crunch if you like. The warmth of the chicken helps the herbs release their fragrance into the dressing.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with the remaining herbs and serve with lettuce leaves, cucumber spears and beans for wrapping and scooping. Choose fewer chilli flakes in the dressing if you'd like a gentler, less fiery version. This larb is nicest eaten shortly after mixing, while the herbs are still fresh and fragrant.

tips: Check the chicken reaches 74°C in the centre and no raw-looking bits remain before taking it off the heat.
A common mistake is browning the mince like a stir-fry; keep the pan at medium-high with the water added so the chicken steams and stays soft instead of crisping.
Red onion gives this larb a lighter, brighter flavour than the shallot used in the beef version - don't swap it back if you want that lift.
Start with less chilli flakes and taste before adding more, especially if serving to those who prefer things milder.
storage: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently until piping hot throughout (74°C) before eating, or serve cold from the fridge; the herbs are best added fresh if making ahead. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
